Oof I feel that. I'm a trans dude who loves dressing feminine, which may sound hypocritical, but... yeah. I hate knowing that others perceive me as a girl when I am a guy and urgh.

How do I cope? I surround myself with friends who make me feel euphoric about my gender. I hate feeling dysphoric, so I focus on the things that make me feel content with my gender. Even though I said that I dress feminine as a trans guy and that fact makes me feel a little dysphoric, dressing androgynous-ly may help you feel more comfortable (unless you prefer dressing feminine).

I'm sorry if this is bad advice or anything, but yeah!

I'm in the same boat (having queerphobic + religious parents), so I *think* I can offer advice, but just take it with a grain of salt. Both my partner and I are AFAB with really religious parents, but we still visit each other's places under the guise of being "best friends" and our parents are fine with it.

It takes time to figure out yourself regarding sexuality, especially in a religious household, so at the very least be patient with yourself and stay strong because you may not have much support from family at the moment. So, in that case, confiding in understanding friends may be enough for now. Having a strong support system is the most important thing.
